sources.actualHeading: デジタル大辞泉: ほう【俸】［漢字項目］
sources.inspection: The actual character entry identifies ホウ and official allowances/pay, with 俸給 and 年俸 among the examples. 精選版 日本国語大辞典 separately describes official remuneration under the noun ほう【俸】.
sources.disposition: Supports the source reading and official-pay association, not a rule restricting every compound to government employees or evidence that the standalone noun is ordinary conversational vocabulary.
sources.limits: The page also contains 普及版 字通's historical analysis, extra 字訓 and damaged gaiji images. Do not mix those extra readings into the frozen metadata or claim to have resolved the complete historical derivation. No unseen gaiji are transcribed.

sources.actualHeading: デジタル大辞泉: ねん‐ぽう【年俸】
sources.inspection: Defines remuneration set on an annual basis or one year's remuneration. The explicit pronunciation note rejects ねんぼう. The 精選版 日本国語大辞典 entry independently gives ねん‐ぽう and the annual-pay sense.
sources.disposition: A useful unlinked comparison for annual pay and the actual ポウ pronunciation in this compound. It does not establish the exact installment schedule, net pay, included bonuses, or a new metadata reading ポウ.
sources.limits: The separate 年俸制 preview is not a full independently inspected entry. No legal/payroll generalization is adopted from it.

sources.actualHeading: 精選版 日本国語大辞典: ほう‐きゅう‥キフ【俸給】
sources.inspection: The actual entry includes remuneration for official duties and, more generally, wages paid to employees of companies and similar organizations. This agrees with frozen JMdict 1515280's salary, especially public employees, sense.
sources.disposition: Candidate direct ホウ + キュウ support, with an official-pay association but no government-only rule. Salary overlap requires checking 給料 and 給与, not manufacturing mutually exclusive semantic compartments.
sources.limits: The returned デジタル大辞泉, 字通 and Britannica sections contained headings/attribution without definitions; they are not verified definitions. Encyclopedia excerpts belong to other entries and are not adopted as evidence of modern legal usage, Latin etymology or strict historical employee categories.

limits: Exact heading/sense inspection and coordinator evidence, not independent review, native-speaker certification, usage-frequency measurement or a completed teaching draft.
